# Results — Study 412 (Symmetrical Triangle)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The technician claim — **a
symmetrical triangle is a continuation figure: when price breaks out of the converging
range it keeps going that way** — tested with the closest **mechanical** definition on
daily OHLC across SPY + a 29-name large-cap basket. We fit swing-pivot trendlines, require
a genuine contraction toward an apex, take the **confirmed** breakout, and measure the
signed forward return against a **random-day base rate** (HAC *t* on the excess +
permutation placebo + costs + a direction split). Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV (`auto_adjust=True`), 30 long-listed US large-caps incl. SPY (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-18 (**21.5** years; **161,970** bars across names) |
| As-of | 2026-06-18 (last bar in the cached panel) · fingerprint **`fd7f2494cbf5`** |
| Detector | swing pivots (`scipy.find_peaks`, ATR-prominence) → upper/lower trendline fit; require converging + symmetric slopes + a real range contraction; **confirmed** breakout when the close pierces the projected trendline |
| Events | **291** confirmed symmetrical-triangle breakouts (**163** up, **128** down) |
| Timing / costs | signal at close of *t*; enter **1 day later** (no look-ahead); hold 1/5/20/60 days; **2 bps** one-way × 2 legs |

> **Chart figures are partly subjective — stated up front.** No two chartists draw the same
> triangle. We test the *closest mechanical definition* (objective swing pivots + trendline
> fits + a contraction filter + a price-pierce confirmation) and report what *that* rule does.
> A hand-drawn triangle could differ; the point of a mechanical detector is that it is
> reproducible and cannot be fit after the fact. **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis):**
> the basket is names still trading in 2026, which mildly tilts any *up*-continuation pattern.

## The signal — forward return after a confirmed breakout vs the random-day base rate

Signed by the breakout direction (long an up-breakout, short a down-breakout). The base rate
is a matched random-day draw from the same name (same direction), so the **excess** strips out
the instrument's own drift. The *t* is a **Newey-West HAC** *t* of the excess against zero;
the placebo *p* is the share of 20,000 label shuffles whose excess beats the observed one.

| horizon | n | win-rate | signal | base rate | **excess** | HAC *t* (excess) | HAC *t* (signal) | placebo *p* | net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 291 | 49.8% | −0.049% | +0.012% | **−0.061%** | −0.45 | −0.53 | 0.672 | −0.089% |
| 5-day  | 291 | 53.3% | −0.024% | −0.155% | **+0.131%** | +0.44 | −0.11 | 0.327 | −0.064% |
| 20-day | 291 | 51.9% | −0.415% | −0.367% | **−0.048%** | −0.07 | −0.97 | 0.529 | −0.455% |
| 60-day | 291 | 50.2% | +0.682% | +0.593% | **+0.089%** | +0.09 | +1.03 | 0.470 | +0.642% |

Read it plainly. **At no horizon does the excess clear — or come anywhere near — the desk's
*t* ≥ 2 bar** (the largest |HAC *t*| on the excess is **0.45**). The win-rate hugs **50%** (the
coin flip), the permitted-luck placebo *p* never drops below **0.33**, and the small positive
signal at 60 days (+0.68%) is fully explained by the random-day base rate (+0.59%) — i.e. by the
market's own 60-day drift, **not** by the triangle. A confirmed symmetrical-triangle breakout, on
the closest mechanical definition, is **statistically indistinguishable from buying a random day.**

## Costs — there is nothing for costs to eat

Each confirmed breakout is a round trip; we charge **2 bps one-way × 2 legs**. Because the gross
edge is already ~zero, the net column is simply negative wherever the gross signal is weak. There
is no break-even cost to quote: the signal does not clear zero on the excess to begin with.

## Direction split — the "continuation" myth check

Split the events by breakout direction. The folklore says **both** should *continue* (up-breakouts
rise, down-breakouts fall further). Here is the raw (un-baselined) signed mean by direction:

| horizon | up-breakout mean | up win% | up *t* | down-breakout mean | down win% | down *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −0.112% | 47.2% | −0.79 | +0.032% | 53.1% | +0.27 |
| 5-day  | +0.050% | 54.6% | +0.19 | −0.118% | 51.6% | −0.30 |
| 20-day | −0.138% | 53.4% | −0.27 | −0.766% | 50.0% | −0.93 |
| 60-day | **+3.894%** | 58.9% | **+3.38** | **−3.407%** | 39.1% | **−2.73** |

This is the trap, and the one number a believer would wave around. At **60 days** the *up*-breakout
group is **+3.9% (t = 3.38)** and the *down*-breakout group is **−3.4% (t = −2.73)** — looks like
roaring continuation! But it **isn't the triangle**: it is **market beta over a 60-day window**.
Over 60 trading days the broad market drifts *up*, so anything you call "long" rises and anything
you call "short" falls — regardless of the figure. The proof is the excess column above: once you
subtract the **matched random-day** return (which carries exactly that 60-day drift), the triangle's
contribution collapses to **+0.089% at *t* = 0.09**. The continuation is the calendar, not the chart.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel where we *splice in* real symmetrical triangles and then **plant** a known
post-breakout continuation drift, the detector + inference behave exactly as they must:

| planted edge | events | signal (20d) | excess (20d) | HAC *t* (excess) | HAC *t* (signal) | placebo *p* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 316 | −0.60% | +0.12% | +0.21 | −1.67 | 0.409 | 43% |
| **+0.20** (large planted continuation) | 228 | +2.45% | **+4.06%** | **+5.79** | **+5.47** | **0.000** | 66% |

With **no** planted edge the excess sits at *t* ≈ 0.2 and the win-rate is below 50% (it does **not**
manufacture significance from noise). With a large planted continuation the harness lights up
cleanly (excess *t* = **5.79**, *p* = 0.000, win 66%). The measurement is unbiased — so the real-tape
*t* ≈ 0 is a genuine **null**, not a detector that is blind to edges.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Across 291 confirmed breakouts on 21.5 years of daily tape, the excess over a
  matched random-day base rate **never clears |*t*| = 0.5** at any horizon (1/5/20/60 days), the
  win-rate sits at ~50%, and the permutation placebo *p* stays ≥ 0.33. The synthetic control proves
  the engine *can* detect a planted continuation (*t* = 5.79) — so finding nothing here is a real
  null, not a blind harness. This is the expected, honest outcome for classic chart-pattern folklore.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no gross edge to deploy; the net column is negative wherever the
  signal is weak, and the only positive raw number (60-day) is just the market's own drift that the
  base rate already captures. Nothing survives costs because nothing survives *zero*.
- **"Continuation figure"? — BUSTED.** The headline-grabbing up/down asymmetry at 60 days (+3.9% vs
  −3.4%) is **market beta over a long window**, not the triangle: it vanishes (excess *t* = 0.09) the
  moment you subtract a matched random-day return. On the closest mechanical definition, a
  symmetrical-triangle breakout is a **50/50 coin flip**.
